_schema_meta.supersedes: the implicit schema 1.0 declared by token_dictionary.ng.v1.1.json _metadata.schema_version
_schema_meta.description: Field semantics for token_dictionary artifacts at schema_version 2.0 — the Symptom Vocabulary 2.0 foundation. This file is the prose contract; schema/token_dictionary.v2.schema.json is the machine-validatable one and is executed in CI by tools/validate_vocabulary.py. Where the two disagree, the machine schema is authoritative and the disagreement is a defect.
locked_principles: No PHI fields — no name, dob, phone, email, address, no free-text user input, no assessment data
Existing token IDs are immutable. A token is deprecated and replaced, never renamed or removed
Clinical identity and search metadata are separate objects. Rules and scoring may read clinical_identity only
Aliases are search phrases, not tokens. An alias has no entry of its own and can never be scored
New schema 2.0 metadata is search/input metadata. It must not affect scoring unless a later clinically reviewed, versioned rules release explicitly consumes it
The six schema 1.0 token arrays remain present, required and order-stable so schema 1.0 consumers keep working unchanged
Artifact is immutable after publish — never overwrite a versioned file
The vocabulary never performs fuzzy matching. Ambiguity is reported, never guessed

versioning_decision.artifact_id_unchanged_because: Backend keys /config artifacts on `token_dictionary`, Mobile reads config['artifacts']['token_dictionary']['url'], and tests/regression/existing-endpoints.test.ts asserts that key. Renaming the artifact to `vocabulary` would be a gratuitous breaking change to two consumers for a cosmetic gain.
versioning_decision.derivation: Repository policy, kb_schema_v1.0.json _field_definitions.version.constraints: 'Major bump for schema changes, minor for content changes'. token_dictionary.ng.v1.1.json declares schema_version 1.0; this release adds fields, and token_dictionary.ng.v1.1.json _metadata.rules states 'Once locked, tokens cannot be renamed without a schema version bump'. A schema change therefore forces a major artifact bump: 1.1 -> 2.0, with schema_version 1.0 -> 2.0.
versioning_decision.candidate_location_rationale: Published artifacts live at the repository root; that is the directory the data engineer uploads to R2 from. Placing an unapproved candidate there would make an unpublished file indistinguishable from a published one. The candidate keeps the conventional filename but sits under candidate/ until clinical review and engineering-lead approval complete.

schema_1_0_consumers.measured_mobile_surface: lib/core/engine/red_flag_evaluator.dart reads exactly two keys — tokenDictionary['symptom_tokens'] and tokenDictionary['red_flag_tokens'] — each as a List, keeping only String members, to build the valid-input token set. No other key of the token dictionary is read anywhere in the mobile engine.
schema_1_0_consumers.guarantee: A schema 2.0 artifact carries all six legacy arrays with identical membership and identical ordering to its source. A schema 1.0 consumer decoding it into a map and reading those keys observes no difference, and ignores every new top-level key.

schema_2_0_consumers.guarantee: Every token_id in `tokens` is exactly the union of the six legacy arrays, and each entry's `category` names the array it came from. Reading `tokens` and reading the legacy arrays yield the same token set.

_compatibility_contract.unknown_field_policy: Consumers MUST ignore top-level keys and object properties they do not recognise. The machine schema sets additionalProperties:false for validation of artifacts this repository generates; it does not license a consumer to reject an artifact carrying a field it has not been taught.

_field_semantics_legend.clinical_or_search: clinical = may be relied on by rules/red flags/scoring. search_only = input and retrieval metadata. display_only = presentation.
_field_semantics_legend.mobile_may_display: Whether Mobile is permitted to render this value to a patient or caregiver.
_field_semantics_legend.rules_may_reference: Whether a rules artifact may name this field or its values.
_field_semantics_legend.may_affect_scoring: Whether a value here is permitted to change a score, weight, urgency tier or red-flag outcome.

tokens[].token_id.normalization: None. Stored verbatim. The derived search form is tokens[].search.normalized_form.
tokens[].token_id.uniqueness: Globally unique across the whole artifact, across all categories. Duplicate IDs are a hard validation failure.
tokens[].token_id.ordering: Entries are ordered by category in the fixed legacy order (symptom, red_flag, duration, body_area, demographic, severity), and within a category in the exact order of the source legacy array. Ordering is generated, never hand-edited.
tokens[].token_id.duplicate_behavior: Hard failure. No de-duplication, no last-wins.
tokens[].token_id.case_handling: ASCII lowercase only. Any uppercase character is a validation failure.
tokens[].token_id.unicode_handling: ASCII only. Non-ASCII is a validation failure.
tokens[].token_id.punctuation_handling: Underscore is the only permitted separator. Hyphens, spaces and dots are validation failures.
tokens[].token_id.whitespace_handling: No whitespace permitted anywhere in the value.
validation_failures: present in tokens[] but absent from its legacy category array, or the reverse
removal of a token ID that exists in the frozen baseline
tokens[].token_id.backward_compatibility: Immutable forever. token_dictionary.ng.v1.1.json _metadata.rules already locks this. Deprecate and replace instead.

tokens[].category.uniqueness: Not unique. Exactly one category per token — the artifact has no cross-category duplicates and the validator enforces that.
tokens[].category.duplicate_behavior: A token appearing in two legacy arrays is a hard validation failure.
validation_failures: disagreement with the legacy array the token appears in
tokens[].category.backward_compatibility: Derived from schema 1.0 structure; adding a category requires a schema bump.

tokens[].clinical_identity.canonical_tok.allowed_values: A token_id present in this artifact.
tokens[].clinical_identity.canonical_tok.uniqueness: Equal to the entry's own token_id for active tokens.
validation_failures: differs from token_id while status is active
a baseline token moving from active to deprecated without a clinical-review record
tokens[].clinical_identity.status.backward_compatibility: A deprecated token stays in its legacy array so schema 1.0 consumers keep resolving it. Deprecation is a signal to new consumers, not a removal.
tokens[].clinical_identity.status.notes: Deprecation is classified `deprecation_removal` by tools/classify_vocabulary_diff.py and blocks publication pending clinical review.

tokens[].clinical_identity.replaced_by.allowed_values: null, or a token_id present in this artifact.
tokens[].clinical_identity.replaced_by.uniqueness: Many tokens may point at the same successor.
validation_failures: a cycle anywhere in the replacement graph
pointing at a token that is itself deprecated with a null successor
tokens[].clinical_identity.replaced_by.notes: Consumers must NOT auto-substitute replaced_by during scoring. It is a migration pointer for authors and for the picker, not a runtime rewrite rule; silent substitution would change clinical meaning without review.

validation_failures: false on a token referenced by kb symptoms/red_flags or by a rules token
flipping true -> false for a baseline token
tokens[].clinical_identity.scoring_eligi.backward_compatibility: Additive. Every token migrated from 1.1 is true: all 295 are pre-existing clinical tokens.
tokens[].clinical_identity.scoring_eligi.notes: This is the structural guarantee that search metadata cannot leak into scoring. Aliases have no entry, therefore no scoring_eligible flag, therefore no path to a score.

validation_failures: a version newer than the artifact's own version
tokens[].clinical_identity.introduced_in.backward_compatibility: Additive. Computed by diffing token_dictionary.ng.v1.0.json against v1.1 — evidence-derived, not asserted.

tokens[].display.canonical_label.normalization: Stored as authored. Its normalized form is added to search_index for retrieval; the stored value is never rewritten.
tokens[].display.canonical_label.uniqueness: Not required to be unique. Two tokens may legitimately share a label — that is precisely what produces an `ambiguous` result rather than a wrong answer.
tokens[].display.canonical_label.duplicate_behavior: Permitted. Recorded in the token reference report as a label collision and surfaced to reviewers; never auto-resolved.
tokens[].display.canonical_label.case_handling: Preserved verbatim for display. Case-insensitive for search via normalization.
tokens[].display.canonical_label.unicode_handling: Full Unicode permitted. Normalized with NFKC for search only.
tokens[].display.canonical_label.punctuation_handling: Preserved verbatim for display; folded to spaces for search.
tokens[].display.canonical_label.whitespace_handling: No leading/trailing whitespace, no newlines, no tabs, no runs of two or more spaces.
validation_failures: display_safe true while label_source is derived_from_token_id
tokens[].display.canonical_label.notes: In the W2 Step 1 candidate every label is mechanically derived from the token ID and is therefore NOT display-safe. No clinically approved label catalogue exists in this repository yet.

validation_failures: clinically_approved without a non-null review.clinical_reviewer and review.review_date
derived_from_token_id where the label does not equal derive_label_from_token_id(token_id)

tokens[].display.display_safe.backward_compatibility: Additive. Defaults to false, so a consumer that ships before any label is approved shows nothing new.
tokens[].display.display_safe.notes: The single gate Mobile checks before putting a vocabulary label on screen. When false, Mobile must fall back to its own approved display map and must never render the raw token ID to a patient.

validation_failures: any value other than en-NG at schema 2.0
tokens[].display.locale.backward_compatibility: Additive. Adding a locale requires a schema bump so a consumer cannot silently receive text it has no renderer or font coverage for. The existing artifacts carry country 'ng' and English content only; nothing in the current architecture negotiates language.

tokens[].search.normalized_form.allowed_values: Output of normalize(token_id with '_' replaced by ' ').
tokens[].search.normalized_form.normalization: Defined by docs/VOCABULARY_NORMALIZATION_SPEC.md and implemented by tools/vocab/normalize.py. Generated, never authored.
tokens[].search.normalized_form.uniqueness: Not required to be unique. Collisions are legitimate and produce `ambiguous`.
tokens[].search.normalized_form.duplicate_behavior: Recorded in search_index as a multi-candidate entry. Never auto-resolved.
tokens[].search.normalized_form.case_handling: Always lowercase — casefold is part of the pipeline.
tokens[].search.normalized_form.unicode_handling: NFKC applied; diacritics preserved (see the normalization spec).
tokens[].search.normalized_form.punctuation_handling: Folded to single spaces except digit-internal '.' and '/', and digit-internal ',' which is deleted.
tokens[].search.normalized_form.whitespace_handling: Runs collapsed to one ASCII space; ends stripped.
validation_failures: value differs from a fresh normalize(token_id) computation

tokens[].search.aliases.allowed_values: Authored search phrases. Empty array when none are approved.
tokens[].search.aliases.normalization: Stored as authored; matched via normalize(). Exact byte equality is tried first, then the normalized form.
tokens[].search.aliases.uniqueness: Within an entry: unique after normalization. Across entries: duplicates are ALLOWED and deliberately produce `ambiguous` rather than a silent pick. The validator reports every cross-entry collision in the migration report so a reviewer sees it.
tokens[].search.aliases.ordering: Sorted by (normalized form, raw string). Deterministic, so regeneration is byte-stable.
tokens[].search.aliases.duplicate_behavior: Duplicate within an entry after normalization is a hard failure. Duplicate across entries is recorded and resolved as ambiguity at query time.
tokens[].search.aliases.case_handling: Case-insensitive for matching; stored case preserved.
tokens[].search.aliases.unicode_handling: Full Unicode permitted; NFKC-normalized for matching.
tokens[].search.aliases.whitespace_handling: No leading/trailing whitespace, no newlines or tabs, no double spaces.
validation_failures: an alias whose normalized form equals its own entry's normalized_form or canonical label — a no-op that only adds index weight
an alias whose normalized form equals any token_id's normalized form belonging to a DIFFERENT entry, unless the expansion request explicitly records the ambiguity as intended
duplicate after normalization within one entry
an alias added without an approved expansion request
tokens[].search.aliases.backward_compatibility: Additive. Empty in the W2 Step 1 candidate — no approved alias catalogue exists yet.
tokens[].search.aliases.notes: An alias is a way to FIND a token. It is never itself a token, has no ID, and cannot be scored. Mobile must display the resolved token's approved label, never the alias the user typed.

validation_failures: any value other than true at schema 2.0
tokens[].search.search_only.notes: A constant, present so the guarantee is machine-checkable from the artifact itself rather than only from documentation. Changing it would require a schema bump and a clinically reviewed rules release.

tokens[].associations.body_areas.allowed_values: body_area_id values from the top-level body_areas vocabulary, which is itself constrained to body_area_tokens.
tokens[].associations.body_areas.duplicate_behavior: Duplicate within the array is a hard failure.
tokens[].associations.body_areas.backward_compatibility: Additive; empty array when unknown. Empty means 'not yet assigned', never 'no body area'.
tokens[].associations.body_areas.mobile_may_display: Only via the body area's own display_safe label.
tokens[].associations.body_areas.notes: Body area drives picker routing and filtering. It must not be used to weight, gate or escalate a condition.

tokens[].associations.complaint_groups.allowed_values: complaint_group_id values from the top-level complaint_groups vocabulary.
tokens[].associations.complaint_groups.duplicate_behavior: Duplicate within the array is a hard failure.
tokens[].associations.complaint_groups.mobile_may_display: Only via the group's own display_safe label.
tokens[].associations.complaint_groups.notes: complaint_groups is empty in the W2 Step 1 candidate: no approved grouping catalogue exists. The vocabulary is present so Product/Clinical can propose one through the expansion request template.

tokens[].associations.severity_descripto.duplicate_behavior: Duplicate within the array is a hard failure.
tokens[].associations.severity_descripto.notes: Declares which severity words a token may sensibly be qualified by when a user describes it. It does NOT set severity, does not map into kb severity_levels, and does not change any weight or urgency tier. kb severity_levels remains the only clinical severity mechanism and is untouched by W2.

tokens[].associations.duration_descripto.duplicate_behavior: Duplicate within the array is a hard failure.
tokens[].associations.duration_descripto.notes: Same constraint as severity_descriptors. Duration remains clinically expressed through kb duration_note and the question flow, neither of which W2 touches.

validation_failures: reviewed with a null clinical_reviewer or a null review_date
tokens[].review.review_status.notes: not_reviewed on every migrated entry. Migration carries a token forward unchanged; it does not constitute a clinical review of that token, and claiming otherwise would be fabricating an approval.

tokens[].review.clinical_reviewer.allowed_values: Reviewer identity as recorded in the approval record, or null.
tokens[].review.clinical_reviewer.notes: Never populated by tooling. Only a human approval record may set it.

tokens[].review.provenance.allowed_values: Non-empty free text naming where the entry's content came from.
tokens[].review.provenance.notes: Every migrated entry carries 'migrated_from_token_dictionary_v1.1 (<sha256 prefix>)'. An entry with no provenance cannot be published.

body_areas[].allowed_values: body_area_id must be a member of body_area_tokens.
body_areas[].duplicate_behavior: Duplicate body_area_id is a hard failure.
body_areas[].unicode_handling: ID ASCII only; label full Unicode.

complaint_groups[].allowed_values: Empty array until an approved grouping catalogue exists.
complaint_groups[].duplicate_behavior: Duplicate ID is a hard failure.
complaint_groups[].unicode_handling: ID ASCII only; label full Unicode.

search_index.normalized_forms.allowed_values: normalized form -> non-empty array of token_id, in resolver order.
search_index.normalized_forms.uniqueness: Keys unique by construction; values unique within an entry.
search_index.normalized_forms.ordering: Keys sorted ascending by codepoint. Values in resolver order — (matched_via rank, category rank, token_id) — which is a fixed lexicographic sort carrying no clinical priority.
search_index.normalized_forms.duplicate_behavior: A key with more than one token_id denotes an ambiguous form. Consumers must return all candidates and resolve none.
validation_failures: the stored index differs from one regenerated from tokens[]
search_index.normalized_forms.notes: Shipped inside the artifact so every consumer resolves identically offline without re-implementing normalization. Regenerated and byte-compared by the validator.

_default_rule: Every field schema 2.0 adds is search, input or display metadata. None of it may affect scoring, red-flag evaluation, urgency or condition ranking unless a later clinically reviewed, versioned rules release explicitly consumes it — which would itself be a rules schema change, reviewed on its own terms.
_unchanged_by_this_schema: red flag precedence, triggers and the global-before-scoring evaluation order
scoring weights, base weights, demographic and seasonal modifier effects
